title: 18,000-tonne illegal dump in Bickershaw to be cleared

evidence_packet.title: 18,000-tonne illegal dump in Bickershaw to be cleared
evidence_packet.lead: The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs says work is underway to clear the site
evidence_packet.summary: The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs says work is underway to clear the site
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An illegal dump containing about 18,000 tonnes of rubbish is set to be cleared, the government has announced The tip, on Bolton House Road near Bickershaw, Wigan, has built up since 2024 In July 2025, a ten-day fire broke out at the site, forcing local businesses and a school to close The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) has confirmed work is now underway to clear the waste, with specialist teams aiming to remove up to 25 lorry loads each day In August, while campaigning to win the Makerfield seat, outgoing Metropolitan Mayor of Greater Manchester, Andy Burnham said the site was "blighting communities" The now-prime minister said at the time that the clean-up job would start "as soon as possible"

evidence_packet.summary: The Levenshulme community space and garden was ripped out by contractors in August by mistake
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents who were left "devastated" after their community alleyway garden was destroyed in a clearance mix-up have said the neighbourhood has come together to help grow again Council contractors ripped out the garden in Levenshulme in Manchester by mistake in August, following five years of planting and growing by locals They had been responding to a report of overgrown vegetation nearby. title: Photos reveal The Smiths' 'dramatic' Manchester farewell

evidence_packet.title: Photos reveal The Smiths' 'dramatic' Manchester farewell
evidence_packet.lead: Rarely-seen images from what proved to be the iconic band's penultimate show surface 40 years on
evidence_packet.summary: Rarely-seen images from what proved to be the iconic band's penultimate show surface 40 years on
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where the Sex Pistols inspired some of the city's most famous bands and the legendary Factory Records , and where rock giants Kiss made their UK debut And it was where The Smiths, one of Manchester's most iconic bands, played what would prove to be their final farewell to the city on 30 October 1986 Forty years on, rarely-seen photos of the show, taken by then-student Alison Bell show what she said was a "dramatic" and "amazing" night Bell, who had been drawn to Manchester by its music scene as a student and went on to have a successful career in music promotion, said she had been desperate to see the band and the Free Trade Hall show was "the first opportunity I had to see them" Formed by singer Morrissey and guitarist Johnny Marr in 1982, the band were at the peak of their powers at the show, riding high on the success of their third long-player, The Queen Is Dead, which would go on to become widely-regarded as one of the greatest albums of all time

title: Oldham: Murder suspect faces investigation over five burglaries

evidence_packet.title: Oldham: Murder suspect faces investigation over five burglaries
evidence_packet.lead: A man in his 70s was found dead during a search of an address on Whitstable Close
evidence_packet.summary: A man in his 70s was found dead during a search of an address on Whitstable Close
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder while already being investigated over five aggravated burglaries, Greater Manchester Police has said A man in his 70s was found dead during a search of an address on Whitstable Close, in Chadderton, Oldham He is believed to have died between 4 and 7 November, with his death being treated as suspicious. His loved ones have been informed A man in his 30s has been arrested on suspicion of aggravated burglary and murder, and remains in custody for questioning He had already been arrested in relation to five aggravated burglaries between January and October when detectives linked him to the murder case The victims in the burglaries had all been targeted similarly, with the suspect attempting to or gaining entry to their properties before demanding they hand over their bank cards and pin codes, the force said

title: The case against each man accused of abusing woman drugged by husband

evidence_packet.title: The case against each man accused of abusing woman drugged by husband
evidence_packet.lead: The prosecution has been outlining its case against nine men accused of abusing an unconscious woman
evidence_packet.summary: The prosecution has been outlining its case against nine men accused of abusing an unconscious woman
evidence_packet.evidence_text: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had already pleaded guilty to 62 offences against her committed at the home they shared in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Four other men have also admitted sexual offences against her, but the remaining defendants deny all charges and are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Louise Oakley KC, lead counsel for the prosecution, has told the jury that both the husband and the other men were leading "double lives" while secretly fulfilling their "barbaric fantasies" The husband's own abuse against the woman, in her sixties, is believed to have begun in 2004 before he began inviting strangers he met on online chatrooms, swinging websites and messaging apps to join him from about 2023 Here the BBC summarises the allegations against each man standing trial

title: Photos reveal The Smiths' 'dramatic' Manchester farewell

evidence_packet.title: Photos reveal The Smiths' 'dramatic' Manchester farewell
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where the Sex Pistols inspired so
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where the Sex Pistols inspired so
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where the Sex Pistols inspired some of the city's most famous bands and the legendary Factory Records , and where rock giants Kiss made their UK debut And it was where The Smiths, one of Manchester's most iconic bands, played what would prove to be their final farewell to the city on 30 October 1986 Forty years on, rarely-seen photos of the show, taken by then-student Alison Bell show what she said was a "dramatic" and "amazing" night Bell, who had been drawn to Manchester by its music scene as a student and went on to have a successful career in music promotion, said she had been desperate to see the band and the Free Trade Hall show was "the first opportunity I had to see them" Formed by singer Morrissey and guitarist Johnny Marr in 1982, the band were at the peak of their powers at the show, riding high on the success of their third long-player, The Queen Is Dead, which would go on to become widely-regarded as one of the greatest albums of all time

evidence_packet.title: Oldham: Murder suspect faces investigation over five burglaries
evidence_packet.lead: A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder while already being investigated over five aggravated burglaries, Greater Manchester Police has said A man in his 70s was found dead during a search of an address on Whitstable Close, in Chadderton, Oldham He is believed to have died
evidence_packet.summary: A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder while already being investigated over five aggravated burglaries, Greater Manchester Police has said A man in his 70s was found dead during a search of an address on Whitstable Close, in Chadderton, Oldham He is believed to have died
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man has been arrested on suspicion of murder while already being investigated over five aggravated burglaries, Greater Manchester Police has said A man in his 70s was found dead during a search of an address on Whitstable Close, in Chadderton, Oldham He is believed to have died between 4 and 7 November, with his death being treated as suspicious. His loved ones have been informed A man in his 30s has been arrested on suspicion of aggravated burglary and murder, and remains in custody for questioning He had already been arrested in relation to five aggravated burglaries between January and October when detectives linked him to the murder case The victims in the burglaries had all been targeted similarly, with the suspect attempting to or gaining entry to their properties before demanding they hand over their bank cards and pin codes, the force said

evidence_packet.lead: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect h
evidence_packet.summary: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect h
evidence_packet.evidence_text: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had already pleaded guilty to 62 offences against her committed at the home they shared in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Four other men have also admitted sexual offences against her, but the remaining defendants deny all charges and are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Louise Oakley KC, lead counsel for the prosecution, has told the jury that both the husband and the other men were leading "double lives" while secretly fulfilling their "barbaric fantasies" The husband's own abuse against the woman, in her sixties, is believed to have begun in 2004 before he began inviting strangers he met on online chatrooms, swinging websites and messaging apps to join him from about 2023 Here the BBC summarises the allegations against each man standing trial

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man who was once told he might never walk or talk again following a devastating brain injury says stand-up comedy has become the key to his recovery Ben Shevlin was hospitalised after a drunk driver crashed into his moped during a family holiday to Croatia back in 2003 Now aged 44, Shevlin, from Salford, has made a near complete recovery, and has gone on to carve out a career performing stand-up comedy, and even run half-marathons He described the road to recovery as "a long process" but said the best advice he had to offer was to "just keep going" Born in 1982, Shevlin said his childhood was very active, and filled with all kinds of sport, including football, athletics, and cricket He went on to study at Manchester Metropolitan University, and the day after his graduation flew out to Dubrovnik in Croatia for a two-week family holiday

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury Demolition plans revealed for Bury's Mill Gate ahead of regeneration New public squares and modernised shopping are touted for the area Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 20:36, 09 Nov 2026 View 3 Images The Mill Gate shoppi Parts of the Mill Gate shopping centre are proposed to be torn down to make way for a new and improved market space Bury council and developer Bruntwood have released new details about how a £24.1m regeneration of the area could be brought forward . The plan is intended to create ‘better connections’ to and through the world-famous Bury Market, as well as delivering ‘improved shopping streets’ At the heart of the scheme is a new public square which would feature new planting, seating and potentially small commercial units to ‘complement the market’. This would sit in Princess Parade, next to the new Casewells flexi-hall, which is due to open later this month The council wants this to be a ‘safe and welcoming’ area combining ‘everyday use’ with events. Retail units along the stretch are expected to be demolished to create room New pedestrian routes would then connect to the square, running along Minden Parade and Market Parade. For this, parts of the Mill Gate shopping centre’s roof would be demolished along with a portion of the B&M store by the multi-storey car park

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Martyn's Law Venues urged to find 'gaps' in security before Martyn's Law comes into force next year Martyn's campaigning mother Figen Murray is behind the campaign for venues to make better plans to ensure public safety at events Add to preferred sour Almost ten years since Martyn Hett died in the Manchester Arena outrage aged just 29, a new law introduced to protect venues from terror attacks is almost a reality His campaigning mother Figen Murray is behind the campaign for venues to make better plans to ensure public safety at events Now the security industry has designed planning tools to make sure venues identify gaps in security and comply before new law comes into force next year The Terrorism (Protection of Premises) Act 2025 will require public premises where 200 or more individuals may be present to be better prepared and have plans in place to keep people safe in the event of an attack Larger premises and events where 800 or more people will be present will be required to take further steps to reduce their vulnerability to acts of terrorism – such as having CCTV, bag search policies or vehicle checks where appropriate. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stepping Hill Hospital Stepping Hill Hospital is falling apart and patients are suffering - yet again, bosses are having to beg for cash Patients' safety is at risk, they say View 9 Images The safety of patients is at risk, Stepping Hill bosses have w Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 18:51, 09 Nov 2026 Updated 20:59, 09 Nov 2026 The safety of patients is at risk at crumbling Stepping Hill Hospital, NHS bosses say as they urgently appeal – yet again – to the government for cash The Stockport site has seen significant upgrades in recent years – including new multi-million emergency and outpatient departments – but much of the estate is need of major work. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury Demolition plans revealed for Bury's Mill Gate ahead of regeneration New public squares and modernised shopping are touted for the area Add to preferred sources Comments News Hannah Richardson 20:36, 09 Nov 2026 View 3 Images The Mill Gate shoppi Parts of the Mill Gate shopping centre are proposed to be torn down to make way for a new and improved market space Bury council and developer Bruntwood have released new details about how a £24.1m regeneration of the area could be brought forward . The plan is intended to create ‘better connections’ to and through the world-famous Bury Market, as well as delivering ‘improved shopping streets’ At the heart of the scheme is a new public square which would feature new planting, seating and potentially small commercial units to ‘complement the market’. This would sit in Princess Parade, next to the new Casewells flexi-hall, which is due to open later this month The council wants this to be a ‘safe and welcoming’ area combining ‘everyday use’ with events. Retail units along the stretch are expected to be demolished to create room New pedestrian routes would then connect to the square, running along Minden Parade and Market Parade. For this, parts of the Mill Gate shopping centre’s roof would be demolished along with a portion of the B&M store by the multi-storey car park

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Etihad Stadium Manchester City will pay extra £320k a year to the council in new Etihad Campus lease deal The town hall has shared details of its new arrangement with the Blues Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Report Manchester City will pay an extra £320,000 a year to the council for its lease at the Etihad Campus as part of an updated agreement Town hall papers published in August revealed a variation to the lease in light of the changes taking place to the stadium and surrounding land, which has been transformed into a major visitor destination since the ground first opened for the 2002 Commonwealth Games New figures released by the council have revealed it will pocket extra each year from its leases with the football club, with a further £33,000 for the stadium lease, £252,000 for City Square, and £35,680 from land in the new Medlock Square hotel and entertainment zone The extra cash will add to the total amount paid to the council by City, which stood at £6.3m last year, made up of £4.4m in rent, £1.1m from naming rights, and £790,000 from income from Champions League games Lease payments for the stadium and City Square are set to increase in future through inflation-linked increases, while the land lease at Medlock Square includes an annual rent uplift of three per cent and future reviews

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Counter Manchester , the much-anticipated new restaurant from Open Restaurant Group , opens its doors today at 12pm. It is the group’s first opening in Manchester city centre and brings a theatrical approach to dining to the heart of the city Led by acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan, Counter is located in Manchester’s Island Building on John Dalton Street and has 60 covers. It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.summary: Manchester United look increasingly likely to sack head coach Michael Carrick The club opted to stick with Carrick after the side's 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October, with the intention of reassessing the situation during this month's international break Multiple sourc
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester United look increasingly likely to sack head coach Michael Carrick The club opted to stick with Carrick after the side's 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on 25 October, with the intention of reassessing the situation during this month's international break Multiple sources have told BBC Sport that the board remain committed to that process, and that no final decision on Carrick's future has been made However, there is a growing expectation that chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will recommend to minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family for Carrick to be sacked The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday means United, who are 18th in the table, have made their worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years BBC Sport reported in October that the club had sounded out former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann over replacing Carrick

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Etihad Stadium Manchester City will pay extra £320k a year to the council in new Etihad Campus lease deal The town hall has shared details of its new arrangement with the Blues Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Report Manchester City will pay an extra £320,000 a year to the council for its lease at the Etihad Campus as part of an updated agreement Town hall papers published in August revealed a variation to the lease in light of the changes taking place to the stadium and surrounding land, which has been transformed into a major visitor destination since the ground first opened for the 2002 Commonwealth Games New figures released by the council have revealed it will pocket extra each year from its leases with the football club, with a further £33,000 for the stadium lease, £252,000 for City Square, and £35,680 from land in the new Medlock Square hotel and entertainment zone The extra cash will add to the total amount paid to the council by City, which stood at £6.3m last year, made up of £4.4m in rent, £1.1m from naming rights, and £790,000 from income from Champions League games Lease payments for the stadium and City Square are set to increase in future through inflation-linked increases, while the land lease at Medlock Square includes an annual rent uplift of three per cent and future reviews

evidence_packet.evidence_text: 15 ноября 2026 года в 229 The Venue состоится концерт ZLATA OGNEVICH в Лондоне Передавая свою музыку через силу чувств и безупречное вокальное мастерство, ZLATA OGNEVICH давно стала яркой артисткой украинской сцены. Её творческий путь охватывает международные музыкальные конкурсы, выступление на сцене “Евровидения”, многочисленные хиты и годы непрерывного т Последние годы стали для певицы временем особой миссии. Её голос звучал не только со сцены, но и в госпиталях, на благотворительных концертах, волонтерских и прифронтовых локациях, поддерживая тех, кто больше всего нуждался в надежде. Более сотни таких выступлений в Украине и уча Клуб 229 — одна из самых известных концертных площадок британской столицы, расположенная в самом сердце города неподалеку от Regent's Park, в ноябре примет ZLATA OGNEVICH. evidence_packet.title: VOLKANOV
evidence_packet.lead: VOLKANOV at Studio 338
evidence_packet.summary: VOLKANOV в Лондоне! 27 ноября 2026 года в Studio 338 состоится концерт VOLKANOV в Лондоне
evidence_packet.evidence_text: 27 ноября 2026 года в Studio 338 состоится концерт VOLKANOV в Лондоне Первый вечерний туман над Темзой, отражение городских огней на воде, аромат кофе из маленьких лондонских кофейных и спешка многолюдных улиц — всё это обладает удивительной способностью вдруг остановить время и вернуть к самым ценным воспоминаниям. Так рождаются чувства, которые д Лондон — город, где встречаются десятки культур, языков и человеческих историй, где старинные набережные Темзы соседствуют с современными кварталами, а бешеный ритм мегаполиса не мешает беречь особую атмосферу уюта. В конце ноября именно здесь, вдали от дома, искренние композиции Концерты Дмитрия Волканова — это искренняя встреча, где между артистом и слушателями почти не остается дистанции. Стоит только прозвучать первым аккордам, как незнакомые люди начинают улыбаться друг другу, петь в унисон и чувствовать себя большой семьей, которую объединила музыка Когда к концу вечера Лондон окутает прохлада, сцена Studio 338 впервые встретит Дмитрия Волканова. Этот вечер станет особым событием — первым знакомством артиста с лондонской публикой. Вас ждут искренние песни, теплая атмосфера и мощная энергетика! Чтобы попасть на концерт VOLKANOV в Лондоне, покупайте билеты на нашем сайте и в кассах города. Ещё больше концертов в афише Лондона ищите у нас на сайте

evidence_packet.summary: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
